# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 7 THE SCHOOLMASTER’S BRIDE

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Captain Saul, who was the initial bride to arrive at this house?” inquired Nell, while they gathered by the hearth following their evening meal.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0000 }

“Did she belong to the tale I’ve heard tied to this dwelling?” Hugh inquired. “I was told by someone that you could relate it, Captain Saul.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0001 }

“Indeed, yes, I am aware of it. I suppose I am the sole living inhabitant of Seven Gulls at present who is able to recall the schoolmaster’s bride as she appeared upon her arrival on the Island. Although she has been deceased these thirty years, she was a member of that class of women that one fails to ever erase from memory.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0002 }

“Narrate the tale to us,” requested Nell. “It is my desire to discover everything concerning the female inhabitants who resided in this dwelling prior to my arrival.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0003 }

“Well, only three have existed—Elizabeth Russell, along with Mrs. Ned Russell, and the schoolmaster’s bride. Elizabeth Russell was a pleasant, smart little thing, and Mrs. Ned was a pleasant woman, as well. However, they could never compare to the schoolmaster’s bride.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0004 }

“John Tremayne was what the schoolmaster was named. During my sixteenth year, he arrived from the Old Country so he could instruct at the Glen's schoolhouse. He differed greatly from the typical castoffs who traveled to P.E.I. for teaching jobs back then. A majority of those men were smart, intoxicated wretches who imparted the three R’s to pupils while sober, yet thrashed them whenever they weren't. John Tremayne, on the other hand, was an attractive, splendid young man. My father provided him with lodging, and despite a decade separating our ages, he and I became close friends. A great deal of our time was spent reading, strolling, and conversing side by side. I suppose he was familiar with practically every poem ever composed, and as we walked beside the shore during the evenings, he would recite it to me. Father considered it a terrible misuse of hours, though he tolerated it to a degree, trusting that it might discourage my desire to head out to sea. Naturally, nothing was capable of accomplishing THAT—a line of seafaring people produced my mother, making the urge part of my nature. Even so, listening to John reading and declaiming gave me great pleasure. Although nearly six decades have passed, I remain able to recite vast stretches of verse that he taught me. Almost sixty years!”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0005 }

For a short while, Captain Saul held his tongue, staring directly at the burning embers to search through the past. Afterwards, he uttered a sigh and continued with his tale.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0006 }

“I recall encounters with him on the sand-hills one spring night. He appeared somewhat elevated—exactly as you appeared, Dr. Carrow, when you escorted Mistress Carrow inside this evening. The second I beheld you, I recalled him. Furthermore, he informed me that a sweetheart remained back home and that she was travelling out to join him. I was barely pleased at all, being an ill-conditioned young chunk of self-interest; I assumed he would not remain as strong a friend to me once she arrived. However, I possessed sufficient manners to conceal it from him. He shared every detail regarding her with me. Her name was Damaris Leigh, and she would have accompanied him out if not for her elderly uncle. He suffered from illness, and because he had cared for her following her parents' deaths, she refused to abandon him. Yet now he had passed away, and she was travelling out for the purpose of marrying John Tremayne. It was by no means a simple trip for a female in those times. You must remember that no steamers existed.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0007 }

“‘At what time do you look for her?’ I ask.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0008 }

“‘The 20th of June is when she departs on the Royal William,’ he states, ‘meaning mid-July ought to see her arrival. Carpenter Johnson must be put to work by me to construct a dwelling for her. Today brought her letter. Prior to unsealing it, I was aware it contained favorable tidings for me. A few evenings back, she appeared to me.’
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0009 }

“I was unable to comprehend him, and he subsequently clarified—even if my comprehension improved merely a fraction. He claimed to possess a gift—or a curse. Those were his exact terms, Mistress Carrow—a gift or a curse. Which one it was remained unknown to him. He mentioned that a great-great-grandmother belonging to him had possessed it, and she was burned as a witch because of it. He stated that peculiar spells—trances, I believe was the term he assigned to them—overcame him from time to time. Do such things exist, Doctor?”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0010 }

“Certain individuals are undoubtedly prone to trances,” Hugh replied. “This issue falls more under the purview of psychical research rather than medicine. What characterized the trances experienced by this John Tremayne?”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0011 }

“Like dreams,” the old Doctor remarked dubiously.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0012 }

“He claimed he was able to perceive things inside them,” Captain Saul uttered deliberately.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0013 }

“Remember, I am relating to you merely what HE stated—events that were occurring—events that were DESTINED to occur. He mentioned that they occasionally brought him solace and occasionally brought him dread. A quartette of nights prior to this, he had experienced one—entering it as he remained seated, watching the flames. Furthermore, he beheld an ancient chamber in England that was familiar to him, with Damaris Leigh inside it, extending her hands toward him while appearing joyful and pleased. Consequently, he understood that favorable tidings concerning her were coming to him.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0014 }

“A dream—a dream,” the aged Doctor sneered.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0015 }

“Probably—probably,” agreed Captain Saul. “That’s what I remarked to him back then. Thinking that was a great deal more reassuring. I disliked the thought of him perceiving stuff of that nature—it felt truly strange.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0016 }

“‘Negative,’ he states, ‘it was no dream of mine. However, our discussion on this matter ends here. Should you dwell on it too greatly, your friendship toward me will lessen.’”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0017 }

“I informed him that nothing was capable of diminishing my friendship for him. He merely shook his head, however, and says, says he:
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0018 }

“‘Young man, I am aware. Previously, this has caused me to lose companions. I hold no grudge against them. At times, it makes me feel scarcely well-disposed toward my own self. That kind of ability possesses a touch of the divine—though whether it belongs to a benevolent or a malevolent deity, who can tell? And every one of us mortals recoils from coming into excessively intimate touch with a God or a devil.’
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0019 }

“Those were the words he used. I recall them just as if it happened yesterday, even if I was not entirely sure what he intended to say. What is your guess about what he REALLY intended, doctor?”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0020 }

“I question whether he comprehended his own meaning,” Doctor Dave remarked crossly.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0021 }

“It seems I comprehend,” Nell murmured. Lips pressed together and eyes gleaming, she paid attention in her customary manner. Captain Saul allowed himself an appreciative grin prior to continuing his tale.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0022 }

“Well, shortly afterward every single person in the Glen and Seven Gulls was aware that the schoolmaster’s bride was arriving, and they were all delighted since he was held in such high esteem by them. And every person showed interest in his newly built home—THIS house. This location was selected by him for it, as the harbor was visible and the ocean could be heard from here. Out there, he created the garden for his bride, though he was not the one who planted the Lombardies. Mrs. Ned Russell was the one who planted THEM. However, a double line of rose-bushes exists in the garden, which were placed there by the young girls who attended the Glen school for the schoolmaster’s bride. According to him, they were pink like her cheeks, white like her brow, and red like her lips. He had cited poetry to such an extent that I suppose he kind of developed the habit of speaking it as well.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0023 }

“Nearly everyone gave him a small gift to assist with outfitting the home. Upon entering it, the Russells were wealthy and appointed it truly finely, just as you can observe; however, the initial furnishings that entered it were quite simple. Nevertheless, this small home overflowed with love. Quilts, tablecloths, and towels were contributed by the women, while a chest was crafted for her by one man, and a table by another, and so forth. A small basket was even woven for her from the sweet-smelling sand-hill grass by blind old Aunt Margaret Garrick. For many years, it was utilized by the schoolmaster’s wife for storing her handkerchiefs.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0024 }

“Well, finally all was prepared—including the logs in the large hearth prepared to be lit. However, it was not precisely THIS fireplace, even if it stood in the identical spot. Miss Elizabeth installed this one when she remodeled the dwelling fifteen years back. You could have roasted an ox in that large, antique hearth. I have sat in this location and told stories many a time, just as I am doing this evening.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0025 }

Once more a hush fell, as Captain Saul briefly communed with unseen guests whom Nell and Hugh were unable to perceive—the people who had joined him beside that hearth during bygone times, with laughter and wedding happiness gleaming in eyes that had been shut eternally beneath cemetery turf or rolling expanses of ocean for a very long time. In this spot during former nights young ones had tossed merry laughter back and forth. In this place throughout cold winter nights companions had assembled. Dancing, melody, and witty remarks had existed here. Within these walls young men and young women had indulged in dreams. To Captain Saul the tiny dwelling was filled with figures begging not to be forgotten.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0026 }

“July’s opening day marked the completion of the dwelling, at which point the schoolmaster commenced his daily tally. Observing him strolling beside the water, we would remark among ourselves, ‘She’ll soon be with him now.’
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0027 }

“Her arrival was anticipated by mid-July, yet she failed to appear at that time. No one experienced concern. Ships were frequently held up for days and perhaps weeks. The Royal William became one week late—and subsequently two—and subsequently three. And eventually we started feeling terrified, and the fear grew steadily more intense. At last I was unable to endure gazing into John Tremayne’s eyes. Do you know, Mistress Carrow”—Captain Saul dropped his tone—“I used to imagine their appearance was identical to how his ancient great-great-grandmother’s must have appeared while she was being burned to death. He rarely spoke a great deal, but he conducted school like someone dreaming and afterward rushed toward the beach. On numerous nights he paced there between nightfall and daybreak. Folks claimed his sanity was slipping. Everyone had abandoned all hope—the Royal William was late by eight weeks. The time was mid-September and the bride of the schoolmaster had not arrived—would never arrive, in our belief.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0028 }

“A severe gale occurred at that time and persisted for three days, and I walked down to the beach on the evening following its cessation. The schoolmaster was present, resting his folded arms on a large boulder while looking toward the ocean.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0029 }

“Although I addressed him, no response came from his lips. Something invisible to my own vision appeared to hold his gaze. Fixed like the countenance of a corpse, his face showed no life.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0030 }

“'John—John,’ I shouted—just in that manner—just like an alarmed youngster, 'wake up—wake up.’
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0031 }

“That peculiar, dreadful expression appeared to somewhat diminish from his eyes.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0032 }

“His head turned, and his eyes met mine. That face of his has never left my memory—and it never will leave it until the time comes for me to embark on my final journey.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0033 }

“‘Everything is fine, boy,’ he says. ‘I have observed the Royal William rounding East Point. She is going to arrive here before dawn. By tomorrow evening I am going to be seated with my wife next to my very own hearth-fire.’
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0034 }

“Is it your opinion that he actually saw it?” Captain Saul asked suddenly.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0035 }

“God knows,” Hugh uttered quietly. “Immense love alongside immense pain could achieve wonders beyond our understanding.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0036 }

“I have no doubt that he observed it,” Nell declared with conviction.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0037 }

“Fol-de-rol,” Doctor Dave remarked, yet his voice carried less certainty than it normally did.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0038 }

“For, as you are aware,” Captain Saul remarked with gravity, “it was at dawn on the following morning that the Royal William entered Seven Gulls Harbor.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0039 }

“All the people living in the Glen and by the beach gathered at the ancient pier for her arrival. The teacher had kept vigil at that spot through the entire night. A great shout went up from us when she navigated into the waterway.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0040 }

A gleam was in Captain Saul’s eyes. Looking past the present, they beheld the Seven Gulls Harbor as it had been sixty years prior, where a worn, aged vessel voyaged amid the magnificence of the rising sun.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0041 }

“Was Damaris Leigh among those on board?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0042 }

“Indeed—she along with the spouse of the captain. The voyage they endured was terrible—one storm following another—and furthermore, their supplies ran out. Nevertheless, they finally arrived. As Damaris Leigh set foot upon the ancient wharf, John Tremayne held her close—causing the crowd to cease shouting and start weeping. Even I wept, even if, remember, it was many years before I confessed to it. Isn't it strange how boys feel such shame about crying?”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0043 }

“Did Damaris Leigh possess beauty?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0044 }

“Indeed, whether you would term her precise beauty—I—do—not—know,” Captain Saul stated unhurriedly. “In a way, one never advanced enough to question if she possessed good looks or lacked them. It simply was irrelevant. A quality so charming and endearing marked her that loving her became inevitable, nothing less. Nevertheless, she presented an agreeable appearance—large, bright, hazel eyes alongside abundant shiny brown hair, plus a complexion typical of the English. That evening when candles were first lit, John and she wed at our dwelling; all the local folk and those from afar gathered there for the event, and collectively we escorted them to this place later. The fire was kindled by Mistress Tremayne, whereupon we departed, leaving the couple seated right where they were, precisely as John had witnessed during his vision. An uncanny occurrence—an uncanny occurrence! Yet I have observed an enormous amount of uncanny occurrences throughout my life.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0045 }

Captain Saul gave a wise shake of his head.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0046 }

“It is a sweet tale,” Nell remarked, experiencing a sense that she had finally received sufficient sentimentality to content herself. “What was the length of time they spent residing in this place?”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0047 }

“Fifteen years. Like the young scalawag I was, I ran off to sea soon after their marriage. However, every time I arrived back from a voyage, even prior to going home, I’d head for this place and tell Mistress Tremayne all about it. Fifteen happy years! Those two possessed a sort of talent for happiness. If you’ve noticed, some folks are like that. No matter what happened, they COULDN’T remain unhappy for long. Because they was both high-sperrited, they quarrelled once or twice. But laughing in that pretty way of hers, Mistress Tremayne says to me once, says she, 'I felt dreadful when John and I quarrelled, but underneath it all I was very happy because I had such a nice husband to quarrel with and make it up with.’ Afterwards, they relocated to Port Marlow, and Ned Russell purchased this house and brought his bride here. As I remember them, they were a gay young pair. Miss Elizabeth Russell was the sister of Hector. A year or so later, she came to live with them, and she was a creature of mirth, too. Laughing and good times must be sorter SOAKED into the walls of this house. Mistress Carrow—you’re the third bride I’ve seen come here, and the handsomest.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0048 }

Captain Saul managed to present his sunflower praise with the subtle grace of a violet, which Nell displayed with pride. That evening saw her appearing her finest, featuring the bridal rose upon her cheeks alongside the love-light in her eyes; even the stern, aged Doctor Dave bestowed a favorable look upon her, remarking to his wife during their shared journey home that the boy’s red-headed spouse possessed a certain beauty.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0049 }

“It is necessary for me to return to the light,” declared Captain Saul. “This evening has been immensely enjoyable for me.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0050 }

“It is necessary that you visit us frequently,” Nell expressed.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0051 }

“I wonder if you’d offer that invitation if you realized how probable it is that I’ll accept it,” Captain Saul observed with a touch of whimsey.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0052 }

“Which amounts to saying you question whether I am serious,” Nell smiled. “I am, ‘cross my heart,’ just like we said in our school days.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0053 }

“In that case, I will come. It is probable that I will bother you at any time. Furthermore, I will be honored if you come over and see me occasionally, as well. Usually, my only speaking companion is the First Mate, bless his friendly soul. Although he listens extremely well and has forgotten a greater amount than any MacAllister among them ever possessed knowledge of, he does not converse very much. Even though you are young and I am old, I suppose the ages of our souls are nearly identical. As Winifred Tolley would express it, we are both members of the race that knows Joseph.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0054 }

“The group that is acquainted with Joseph?” Nell asked in confusion.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0055 }

“Indeed. Winifred categorizes everyone in the world into two types—the people who understand Joseph and the people who do not. Should an individual more or less agree with you, sharing roughly identical thoughts regarding matters, along with a matching sense of humor—well, in that case, they are part of the people who understand Joseph.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0056 }

“Ah, I see,” cried Nell, comprehension suddenly dawning on her.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0057 }

“It is the phrase—which I continue to place in quote marks—'kindred spirits,' as I once termed it.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0058 }

“Precisely—precisely,” Captain Saul concurred. “Whatever IT may be, we are it. Mistress Carrow, as you arrived this evening, I remarked to myself, 'Indeed, she belongs to the lineage that recognizes Joseph.’ And I felt immensely pleased, because had that not been true, we would have been unable to derive any genuine enjoyment from one another’s presence. I believe the lineage that recognizes Joseph constitutes the salt of the earth.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0059 }

The moon was newly risen as Nell and Hugh accompanied their guests to the door. Seven Gulls Harbor was starting to turn into a realm of dream, glamour, and enchantment—a charmed port where no storm could ever destroy. Down the lane, the Lombardies, as lofty and grave as the sacerdotal figures of a mystic fraternity, were crested with silver.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0060 }

“Lombardies have always been favorites of mine,” Captain Saul stated, gesturing toward them with an elongated arm. “Trees for princesses are what they are. Nowadays, people consider them outdated. They object to their tops dying off and becoming shabby. It is true—it is true, provided you fail to jeopardize your safety each spring by ascending a frail ladder to cut them back. My performing this task for Miss Elizabeth ensured that her Lombardies remained pristine. They held a special place in her heart. Their reserved nature and majestic air appealed to her. Every Tom, Rufus, and Harry is denied their friendship. Mistress Carrow, maples provide companionship, but Lombardies offer high society.”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0061 }

“It is such a lovely evening,” remarked Mrs. Doctor Dave while getting up into the buggy belonging to the Doctor.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0062 }

“The majority of nights possess beauty,” Captain Saul remarked. “However, I must admit that the moon shining upon Seven Gulls leads me to ponder how heaven could offer anything more. Mistress Carrow, the moon serves as a wonderful companion to me. My affection for her dates back as far as my memory goes. As a young lad aged eight, I drifted off to sleep outdoors in the garden during an evening without being noticed. Waking up during the middle of the night, I felt frightened nearly to the point of dying. The shadows and odd sounds that existed were dreadful! Moving was something I did not dare to do. I simply remained huddling and trembling there, a helpless little creature. It felt as though no other person existed on earth besides me, and the world appeared vast. At that moment, I suddenly observed the moon peering at me via the apple branches, resembling a familiar pal. Relief came over me instantly. I stood and journeyed toward the dwelling as courageous as a lion, keeping my gaze upon her. Countless nights have seen me observing her from the deck of my vessel, traversing waters distant from this place. Is there a reason you people fail to command me to pull in my tongue and return to my house?”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0063 }

The merriment of the farewells faded into silence. Strolling hand in hand, Nell and Hugh circled their garden. In the birches' shade, the brook flowing through the corner showed clear, shimmering ripples. Resembling delicate goblets of moonlight, poppies lined its borders. Blossoms that the schoolmaster’s bride had set in the earth cast their fragrance into the dim atmosphere, resembling the grace and benediction of holy days gone by. Halting in the darkness, Nell plucked a stem.
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0064 }

“It gives me pleasure to catch the scent of blossoms when it is night,” she stated. “That is when you truly reach their essence. Oh, Hugh, my dreams of this tiny cottage have all come true. And my heart is filled with joy that others before us have shared a newlyweds’ rendezvous in this place!”
{: #nw-v04-c07-p0065 }
